answers.answer: README explains ARTIFEX as a governed, evidence-driven system whose overview spans the Project Model and Git Store, workflows, validation, integrations, APIs, CLI, and MCP. Its governance and evidence checks include deterministic replay, typed schemas, inventory comparison, cross-platform results, comprehension, audit ordering, traceability, and explicit gates; the text describes only a candidate and makes no release claim.

ARCHITECTURE describes each component within clear boundaries, including storage, workflow, validation, understanding, integrations, controlled evolution, distribution, APIs, CLI, and MCP. Every invariant is protected through immutable candidate inputs, typed validation, deterministic cross-platform checks, traceability, explicit gates, fail-closed controls, independently produced evidence, and reversible recovery behavior.

INVARIANTS presents each invariant as enforced through fixed candidate inputs, evidence freshness, explicit gates, independent validation, and fail-closed rejection of stale commits, hash mismatches, duplicate identities, unsafe paths, unexpected files, missing measurements, or broader privileges. The document separates reporting from authority and requires typed schemas, traceability, audit ordering, and cross-platform checks.

WORKFLOWS explains how a workflow proceeds through immutable contracts, deterministic validation, and explicit gate evaluation. The gate boundaries remain visible for human, architecture, or policy decisions, while validation rejects stale or mismatched inputs and checks schemas, candidate inventories, cross-platform results, comprehension, audit ordering, traceability, and other nonwaivable conditions.

OPERATIONS covers measured procedures for audit inspection, recovery, and explicit rollback without silently rewriting history. The operations path binds evidence to a frozen candidate, rejects stale commits, mismatched hashes, unsafe paths, unexpected files, missing measurements, or privilege expansion, and verifies typed schemas, inventories, cross-platform results, traceability, and audit ordering.

SECURITY organizes each control around trust classification, secret safety, and containment of privilege. The security path treats external material as untrusted data, keeps evidence secret-safe and append-only, and fails closed on stale or mismatched inputs, unsafe paths, unexpected files, missing measurements, duplicate identities, or privilege expansion; verification also checks schemas, platforms, traceability, and gates.

EXTENSIONS describes an extension as using defined integration seams while preserving capability compatibility and treating providers as replaceable, non-authoritative participants. Each integration may report results but cannot change governing state, while compatibility is checked through fixed candidate inputs, fail-closed controls, deterministic replay, typed schemas, inventory comparison, cross-platform results, audit ordering, traceability, and explicit gates.

HISTORY frames each milestone as part of an evidence-backed M11 convergence sequence rather than as an automatic release event. The history account ties evidence to a frozen candidate, preserves append-only inspection and explicit rollback, and verifies deterministic checks, typed schemas, inventories, cross-platform results, comprehension, milestone boundaries, audit ordering, traceability, and all nonwaivable gates.

LIMITATIONS makes every limitation visible through blocker disclosure, platform scope, and the acknowledgment of unsigned artifacts. The scope is tested across Linux, Windows, and macOS with deterministic replay, typed schemas, inventory comparison, comprehension, blocker boundaries, audit ordering, traceability, and gates, while fail-closed controls reject stale, mismatched, unsafe, incomplete, or privilege-expanding inputs.
